verdict.rationale: Elasticsearch is a search/data engine, and while it could theoretically be used to build such analytics via custom logging and dashboards, no evidence pack item describes a built-in feature that tracks top queries, no-result (zero-hit) queries, or click-through rate out of the box. The evidence focuses on vector/hybrid search, serverless deployment, and MCP integration — nothing about search analytics dashboards. missing for 10: any documentation of a built-in search-analytics UI/API tracking top queries, zero-result queries, or CTR.
